statements.text: Brazil is the only country in the Americas where Portuguese is the main language.
Brazil has won the men's football World Cup five times, more than any other country.
Brazil's capital is Rio de Janeiro.
statements.truth: Brasília has been Brazil's capital since 1960. Rio de Janeiro was the capital before that.

statements.text: In parts of northern Norway, the sun doesn't set for weeks in the middle of summer.
Norway's coast is famous for its fjords, long narrow inlets carved out by glaciers.
Norway is a member of the European Union.
statements.truth: Norwegians voted against joining in 1972 and again in 1994. Norway works closely with the EU through the European Economic Area instead.

statements.text: Kenya is named after Mount Kenya, the second-highest mountain in Africa.
The equator runs through Kenya.
Kenya's capital is Mombasa.
statements.truth: Kenya's capital is Nairobi. Mombasa is its biggest port, on the Indian Ocean coast.

statements.text: All of China officially runs on a single time zone, despite the country's huge width.
Papermaking was invented in China around 2,000 years ago.
The Great Wall of China is easy to see from the Moon with the naked eye.
statements.truth: This is a popular myth. The wall is far too narrow to see from the Moon, and it's hard to spot even from low orbit.

statements.text: Iceland has no standing army.
Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was founded in 930 and is one of the oldest in the world.
More than half of Iceland is covered by glaciers.
statements.truth: Glaciers and lakes together cover only about 14% of Iceland. Much of the rest is highland, lava fields and tundra.

statements.text: Japan is made up of more than 14,000 islands.
Japan has more than 100 active volcanoes.
Japan's national flower is the lotus.
statements.truth: Japan has no national flower set in law, but the cherry blossom and the chrysanthemum are its traditional floral symbols.

statements.text: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still largely standing.
Most Egyptians live along the Nile and its delta.
The Nile flows south through Egypt toward the Red Sea.
statements.truth: The Nile flows north through Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean Sea.

statements.text: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never colonised by a Western power.
Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world.
Thailand used to be called Burma.
statements.truth: Thailand was officially called Siam until 1939. Burma is the former name of neighbouring Myanmar.

statements.text: About half of the Netherlands is less than 1 m (3 ft) above sea level, and much of that is below it.
Amsterdam is the capital, but the government sits in The Hague.
Tulips are native to the Netherlands.
statements.truth: Wild tulips come from Central Asia and the region around Türkiye. They reached the Netherlands in the 1500s.

statements.text: Chile is more than 4,000 km (2,500 mi) long but on average less than 200 km (120 mi) wide.
Chile's Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth.
Easter Island belongs to Peru.
statements.truth: Easter Island, also called Rapa Nui, is part of Chile.

statements.text: Canada has the longest coastline of any country.
English and French are both official languages of Canada's federal government.
Most Canadians live in the country's far north.
statements.truth: Most Canadians live in the south, many of them fairly close to the border with the United States.

statements.text: India has the largest population of any country.
Chess is widely believed to come from an ancient Indian game called chaturanga.
Hindi is India's only official language.
statements.truth: Hindi and English are both official languages of the central government, and the constitution recognises 22 scheduled languages.

statements.text: Morocco's al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, is often called the oldest place of learning still in use.
At the Strait of Gibraltar, Morocco is only about 14 km (9 mi) from Spain.
Morocco's capital is Marrakesh.
statements.truth: Morocco's capital is Rabat. Casablanca is the biggest city, and Marrakesh is a famous historic city.

statements.text: Lake Baikal, in Siberia, is the deepest lake in the world.
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world.
At their closest point, Russia and the United States are more than 1,000 km apart.
statements.truth: In the Bering Strait, Russia's Big Diomede Island and the United States' Little Diomede Island are less than 4 km (2.5 mi) apart.

statements.text: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world.
Wild lemurs live naturally only on Madagascar and a few small nearby islands.
Madagascar broke away from South America millions of years ago.
statements.truth: Madagascar separated from mainland Africa, and later from India, many millions of years ago.

statements.text: Two independent countries lie entirely inside Italy: San Marino and Vatican City.
The Po is Italy's longest river.
Pizza Margherita was named after a famous opera singer.
statements.truth: The usual story is that it was named after Queen Margherita of Savoy, who visited Naples in 1889.

statements.text: Indonesia is made up of more than 13,000 islands.
Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizards, live in the wild only in Indonesia.
Most Indonesians live on the island of Borneo.
statements.truth: More than half of Indonesians live on Java, one of the most densely populated islands on Earth.

statements.text: Ethiopia uses its own calendar, which runs about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.
The coffee plant is believed to have come originally from Ethiopia.
Ethiopia has a long coastline on the Red Sea.
statements.truth: Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea became independent in 1993.

statements.text: Mexico City is built on the bed of a former lake, Lake Texcoco.
Mexico officially recognises 68 Indigenous languages.
Mexico's official name is the Republic of Mexico.
statements.truth: Mexico's official name is the United Mexican States (Estados Unidos Mexicanos).

statements.text: Finland has roughly 188,000 lakes.
Finnish isn't related to most European languages. One of its closest relatives is Estonian.
The sauna was invented in Sweden.
statements.truth: "Sauna" is a Finnish word, and Finnish sauna culture is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

statements.text: The Great Barrier Reef, off Australia's northeast coast, is the world's largest coral reef system.
Canberra was built as Australia's capital partly as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
Australia has more people than California.
statements.truth: Australia has about 28 million people. California alone has about 39 million.

statements.text: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 1400s.
Lake Titicaca, on Peru's border with Bolivia, is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.
Peru's currency is the peso.
statements.truth: Peru's currency is the sol.

statements.text: Istanbul stretches across two continents, Europe and Asia.
Saint Nicholas, who inspired the legend of Santa Claus, was born in what is now Türkiye.
Istanbul is the capital of Türkiye.
statements.truth: The capital is Ankara. Istanbul is the largest city.

statements.text: In 1893, New Zealand became the first self-governing country to let women vote in national elections.
New Zealand has no native land snakes.
The kiwi, New Zealand's national bird, can fly short distances.
statements.truth: Kiwi are flightless. Their wings are tiny and hidden under their feathers.

statements.text: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated independent country in the world.
The Mongol Empire, founded by Genghis Khan, became the largest connected land empire in history.
Mongolia has a coastline on the Pacific Ocean.
statements.truth: Mongolia is landlocked, sitting between Russia and China.

statements.text: Greece has around 6,000 islands and islets, but only about 227 are inhabited.
The marathon race is named after Marathon, a town in Greece.
The ancient Olympic Games were held in Athens.
statements.truth: The ancient Games were held at Olympia, in the western Peloponnese. Athens hosted the first modern Games in 1896.

statements.text: Vietnam is one of the world's biggest coffee exporters.
Hạ Long Bay is dotted with around 1,600 limestone islands and islets.
Ho Chi Minh City is Vietnam's capital.
statements.truth: The capital is Hanoi, in the north. Ho Chi Minh City is the largest city.

statements.text: South Africa has 12 official languages.
South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
Table Mountain overlooks Johannesburg.
statements.truth: Table Mountain overlooks Cape Town, more than 1,200 km (750 mi) from Johannesburg.

statements.text: Argentina is the eighth-largest country in the world by area.
Aconcagua, in Argentina, is the highest mountain outside Asia.
The tango was born in Brazil.
statements.truth: The tango grew up in the late 1800s around the Río de la Plata, in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

statements.text: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
Bern is officially called Switzerland's "federal city" rather than its capital.
The Matterhorn is Switzerland's highest mountain.
statements.truth: Switzerland's highest peak is the Dufourspitze, at 4,634 m. The Matterhorn is 4,478 m.

statements.text: Sri Lanka's tea is still sold as 'Ceylon tea', after the island's old name.
Sigiriya in Sri Lanka is an ancient rock fortress on top of a rock about 180 m (590 ft) high.
True cinnamon originally comes from South America.
statements.truth: True cinnamon, also called Ceylon cinnamon, is native to Sri Lanka.

statements.text: Vienna's Tiergarten Schönbrunn, opened in 1752, is the oldest zoo still running in the world.
Austria's Eisriesenwelt is the largest ice cave in the world.
Vienna's famous Sachertorte is a lemon sponge cake.
statements.truth: The Sachertorte is a chocolate sponge cake with apricot jam and a chocolate glaze, credited to Vienna's Franz Sacher.

statements.text: Haiti declared independence in 1804, becoming the first sovereign state in the Caribbean.
The Citadelle Laferrière in Haiti is one of the largest fortresses in the Americas.
Haiti's official languages are French and Spanish.
statements.truth: Haiti's official languages are French and Haitian Creole.

statements.text: Togo's Koutammakou landscape is famous for its traditional mud tower-houses, a national symbol of Togo.
Togo was once part of a German protectorate called Togoland.
Togo's capital, Lomé, is in the far north of the country, far from the coast.
statements.truth: Lomé is on the Gulf of Guinea coast, right next to the border with Ghana.

statements.text: Victoria Falls, on Zambia's border with Zimbabwe, is known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'.
Every year millions of straw-coloured fruit bats gather in Zambia's Kasanka National Park.
Zambia was formerly called Southern Rhodesia.
statements.truth: Zambia was Northern Rhodesia. Southern Rhodesia is the former name of Zimbabwe.

statements.text: The desert planet Tatooine in the first Star Wars film was filmed in Tunisia.
The ancient city of Carthage stood on the shore of the Lake of Tunis, in what is now Tunisia.
Tunisia's capital, Tunis, was named after the country.
statements.truth: It is the other way round: Tunisia is named after its capital city, Tunis.

statements.text: Sweden's Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi is rebuilt from ice and snow every winter.
Sweden's 'allemansrätten', or everyman's right, lets people hike across and even camp for a night or two on other people's land.
All the Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.
statements.truth: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.

statements.text: Venezuela's Angel Falls is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall.
Near Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo, the Catatumbo lightning storms flash on 140 to 160 nights a year.
The name Venezuela means 'Little Spain'.
statements.truth: Venezuela means 'Little Venice'. Explorers were reminded of Venice by houses built on stilts over the water.

statements.text: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.
Vostok 1, which carried Yuri Gagarin into space, was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
The wild ancestor of the apple comes from the hills of Spain.
statements.truth: The main wild ancestor of today's apple, Malus sieversii, grows in the mountains of Central Asia, including Kazakhstan.

statements.text: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.
Lesotho is the only independent country that lies entirely above 1,000 m (3,300 ft).
The traditional Basotho hat, the mokorotlo, is shaped like a crescent moon.
statements.truth: The mokorotlo is a conical straw hat, said to be modelled on the shape of a mountain.

statements.text: The giant sable antelope, a national symbol of Angola, is found only in Angola.
Angola's Kalandula Falls are among the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume.
Angola has no coastline and is surrounded entirely by other countries.
statements.truth: Angola lies on the Atlantic coast of southern Africa, and its capital, Luanda, is a port on the ocean.

statements.text: The United States bought Alaska from Russia in 1867.
Yellowstone, established in 1872, is considered the first national park in the world.
The Statue of Liberty was designed by an American sculptor.
statements.truth: The Statue of Liberty was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi and was a gift from France.

statements.text: The shore of the Dead Sea, on Jordan's western border, is the lowest land on Earth.
Petra's famous buildings are carved directly into pinkish sandstone cliffs.
Jordan has no coastline at all.
statements.truth: Jordan has a short coastline on the Gulf of Aqaba, at its port city of Aqaba.

statements.text: The cravat, ancestor of the necktie, became fashionable in France in the 1660s thanks to the knotted neck scarves of Croatian soldiers.
Croatia has more than 1,000 islands and islets along its Adriatic coast.
The Dalmatian dog breed is named after a region of Hungary.
statements.truth: The Dalmatian is named after Dalmatia, a region of Croatia on the Adriatic coast.

statements.text: In the name Burkina Faso, 'Burkina' means 'upright' and 'Faso' means 'fatherland'.
Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, a festival of African cinema held every two years.
Burkina Faso used to be called Dahomey.
statements.truth: Burkina Faso was called Upper Volta until 1984. Dahomey is the former name of neighbouring Benin.

statements.text: Spain's national anthem, the Marcha Real, has no official lyrics.
At La Tomatina, a festival in the town of Buñol, people throw tomatoes at each other.
The Sagrada Família in Barcelona was completed in 1926.
statements.truth: Construction began in 1882 and has gone on for well over a century. Gaudí died in 1926 with the church far from finished.

statements.text: Lake Malawi is thought to have more species of fish than any other lake in the world.
Malawi is nicknamed 'the Warm Heart of Africa'.
Lake Malawi is shallow, nowhere deeper than about 50 m (160 ft).
statements.truth: Lake Malawi is more than 700 m (2,300 ft) deep, making it one of the deepest lakes in the world.

statements.text: Colombia's Caño Cristales is nicknamed the 'river of five colours'.
Colombia has coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
Colombia is named after its first president.
statements.truth: Colombia is named after Christopher Columbus.

statements.text: Eswatini's Umhlanga, or Reed Dance, is a yearly ceremony in which thousands of young women bring reeds to the Queen Mother.
Eswatini was known as Swaziland until 2018.
Mbabane is Eswatini's only capital.
statements.truth: Eswatini has two capitals: Mbabane is the administrative capital, and Lobamba is the legislative capital, home to the parliament.

statements.text: The frankincense trees and ancient incense-trade sites of Oman's Dhofar region are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Oman's Musandam Peninsula is separated from the rest of the country by the United Arab Emirates.
Oman's monsoon season turns the north of the country green.
statements.truth: The khareef monsoon greens the south of Oman, in the Dhofar region around Salalah.

statements.text: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa.
The Gambia is almost completely surrounded by Senegal, apart from its short Atlantic coast.
The Gambia is named after its capital city.
statements.truth: The country's name comes from the Gambia River, which flows through the middle of it. The capital is Banjul.

statements.text: The Sundarbans, shared by Bangladesh and India, is the largest mangrove forest in the world.
Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh has a sea beach about 120 km (75 mi) long.
International Mother Language Day honours a language movement in Nepal.
statements.truth: The day honours the Bengali Language Movement of 1952, in what is now Bangladesh.

statements.text: Spanish and Guaraní are both official in Paraguay, making Guaraní one of the last widely used Indigenous national languages in South America.
The Itaipu Dam, shared by Paraguay and Brazil, is one of the largest hydroelectric plants in the world.
Paraguay has a coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.
statements.truth: Paraguay is landlocked, bordered by Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia.

statements.text: Zimbabwe takes its name from Great Zimbabwe, a medieval stone city in the country's south-east.
Lake Kariba, shared by Zimbabwe and Zambia, is the world's largest artificial lake by volume.
Zimbabwe has three official languages.
statements.truth: Zimbabwe's constitution recognises 16 official languages.

statements.text: San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic, traditionally founded in 301.
San Marino is completely surrounded by Italy.
San Marino's capital city sits on top of Monte Bianco.
statements.truth: The City of San Marino sits on top of Monte Titano.

statements.text: A gold harp on a blue background is Ireland's coat of arms.
Newgrange, a passage tomb in Ireland built around 3100 BC, is older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids.
Halloween grew out of an old Irish festival called Beltane.
statements.truth: Halloween's roots lie in Samhain, a Gaelic festival marking the end of the harvest. Beltane is a spring festival.

statements.text: Liberia was founded in the 1800s as a settlement for freed African Americans.
Liberia's flag, with 11 stripes and a single star, closely resembles the flag of the United States.
Liberia's capital, Monrovia, is named after a local river.
statements.truth: Monrovia is named after James Monroe, the fifth US president, who supported the settlement.

statements.text: Lake Assal in Djibouti is the lowest point in Africa, about 155 m (509 ft) below sea level.
Djibouti sits on the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, which links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
Djibouti's official languages are Arabic and English.
statements.truth: Djibouti's official languages are French and Arabic.

statements.text: In 301, Armenia became the first country to adopt Christianity as its state religion.
The world's oldest known leather shoe, about 5,500 years old, was found in a cave in Armenia.
The Armenian alphabet was copied unchanged from the Greek alphabet.
statements.truth: The Armenian alphabet was created by the scholar Mesrop Mashtots around 405 AD.

statements.text: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.
Barbuda's Codrington Lagoon is home to the largest colony of magnificent frigatebirds in the world.
Antigua was named by early Dutch explorers.
statements.truth: Christopher Columbus named the island Santa María de la Antigua on his 1493 voyage.

statements.text: The saxophone was invented by Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.
Brussels' famous Manneken Pis statue is more than 10 m (33 ft) tall.
statements.truth: The Manneken Pis is tiny, only about 55.5 cm (22 in) tall.

statements.text: The Maya city of Copán in Honduras is famous for its long Hieroglyphic Stairway.
Honduras' Bay Islands lie on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the second-longest reef system in the world.
Honduras has no coastline on the Pacific Ocean.
statements.truth: Honduras has a short Pacific coastline on the Gulf of Fonseca, as well as its long Caribbean coast.

statements.text: São Tomé and Príncipe is the second-smallest country in Africa.
The equator passes through Ilhéu das Rolas, a small island just south of São Tomé.
São Tomé and Príncipe was a Dutch colony.
statements.truth: São Tomé and Príncipe was a Portuguese colony and became independent in 1975.

statements.text: Timor-Leste shares the island of Timor with Indonesia.
Timor-Leste uses the US dollar as its currency.
Timor-Leste's official languages are Malay and English.
statements.truth: Timor-Leste's official languages are Portuguese and Tetum (Tetun).

statements.text: The Congo River is the deepest river in the world, more than 220 m (720 ft) deep in places.
The okapi, a forest animal related to the giraffe, lives in the wild only in the DR Congo.
The DR Congo is landlocked, with no access to the ocean.
statements.truth: The DR Congo has a short Atlantic coastline, about 37 km (23 mi) long, at the mouth of the Congo River.

statements.text: Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world by surface area.
On 6 March 1957, Ghana became the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence.
Kente cloth comes originally from Kenya.
statements.truth: Kente is a woven cloth from Ghana, made by the Akan and Ewe peoples.

statements.text: Benin is a heartland of Vodun, and holds a national Vodun holiday every year on 10 January.
The Royal Palaces of Abomey, built by the kings of Dahomey, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
English is the official language of Benin.
statements.truth: French is Benin's official language, and dozens of local languages such as Fon and Yoruba are widely spoken.

statements.text: Liechtenstein abolished its army in 1868.
Liechtenstein is doubly landlocked: it is surrounded only by countries that are themselves landlocked.
Liechtenstein uses the euro as its currency.
statements.truth: Liechtenstein uses the Swiss franc.

statements.text: Santo Domingo is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas.
Pico Duarte in the Dominican Republic is the highest mountain in the Caribbean.
Merengue music comes originally from Cuba.
statements.truth: Merengue is a music genre from the Dominican Republic.

statements.text: Ushguli in Georgia is one of the highest continuously inhabited settlements in Europe.
The Georgian language is written in its own alphabet, called Mkhedruli.
Georgian wine is traditionally aged in wooden barrels buried under the floor.
statements.truth: Georgia's traditional wine vessel is the qvevri, a large clay jar buried in the ground.

statements.text: The coco de mer palm of the Seychelles produces the largest seed of any plant.
Aldabra, an atoll in the Seychelles, is home to around 180,000 giant tortoises.
The Seychelles is made up of just three islands.
statements.truth: The Seychelles has 115 islands in the Indian Ocean.

statements.text: The Lut Desert in Iran has recorded some of the hottest ground temperatures on Earth, up to 70.7 °C (159 °F).
Qanats, underground channels that carry water from hills to farms, were developed in ancient Iran.
Persian, Iran's main language, is a form of Arabic.
statements.truth: Persian is an Indo-European language, though it is written in a script based on Arabic.

statements.text: The Great Blue Hole off Belize is a giant underwater sinkhole about 300 m (1,000 ft) across.
Belize is the only country in Central America where English is the official language.
Belize's Cockscomb Basin was set up as a sanctuary for pandas.
statements.truth: The Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary was created to protect jaguars.

statements.text: Malta's Ġgantija temples, on the island of Gozo, are older than the pyramids of Egypt.
Maltese grew out of Sicilian Arabic but is written in the Latin alphabet.
Malta is made up of a single island.
statements.truth: Malta is an archipelago. Its three main islands are Malta, Gozo and Comino.

statements.text: Rwanda is known as the 'land of a thousand hills'.
On the last Saturday of each month, Rwandans take part in Umuganda, a morning of community work.
Rwanda's mountain gorillas live in the Serengeti.
statements.truth: Rwanda's mountain gorillas live in Volcanoes National Park, in the Virunga Mountains.

statements.text: Bhutan measures its progress with 'Gross National Happiness'.
Bhutan's Paro Taktsang, or Tiger's Nest, monastery clings to a cliff about 900 m (3,000 ft) above the valley.
Bhutan's national animal is the snow leopard.
statements.truth: Bhutan's national animal is the takin, a sturdy mountain goat-antelope.

statements.text: Botswana's Okavango River floods into the Kalahari and spreads out into a vast inland delta instead of reaching the sea.
Botswana's Makgadikgadi Pan is one of the largest salt flats in the world.
Botswana's currency is called the rand.
statements.truth: Botswana's currency is the pula, a Setswana word that means 'rain'.

statements.text: Saint Lucia is named after Saint Lucy of Syracuse, an early Christian saint.
The Pitons, two volcanic spires on Saint Lucia, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Saint Lucia was only ever ruled by Spain.
statements.truth: England and France fought 14 times for control of Saint Lucia.

statements.text: The Island of Mozambique, which gave the country its name, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Mozambique joined the Commonwealth in 1995, even though it was never a British colony.
Swahili is Mozambique's official language.
statements.truth: Portuguese is Mozambique's official language.

statements.text: Lake Ohrid is one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes, with more than 200 species found nowhere else.
Mother Teresa was born in Skopje.
Lake Ohrid lies entirely within North Macedonia.
statements.truth: Lake Ohrid is shared by North Macedonia and Albania.

statements.text: Zuma Rock, a huge natural monolith in Nigeria, appears on the 100-naira banknote.
More than 500 native languages are spoken in Nigeria.
Lagos is Nigeria's capital.
statements.truth: Abuja has been Nigeria's capital since 1991. Lagos is its biggest city.

statements.text: The Philippines is made up of more than 7,600 islands.
The Chocolate Hills on Bohol are more than 1,000 grassy, cone-shaped hills that turn brown in the dry season.
The Philippines is named after a Spanish explorer.
statements.truth: The Philippines is named after King Philip II of Spain.

statements.text: Uganda's Bwindi Impenetrable Forest is home to about half of the world's mountain gorillas.
The White Nile flows out of Lake Victoria at Jinja, Uganda.
Uganda's flag features a lion.
statements.truth: Uganda's flag shows a crested crane in a white circle at its centre.

statements.text: Parts of the Pirates of the Caribbean films were shot on Saint Vincent.
La Soufrière, the volcano on Saint Vincent, had an eruption lasting from December 2020 to April 2021.
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a single island.
statements.truth: It is an archipelago: the main island of Saint Vincent plus a chain of smaller islands, the Grenadines.

statements.text: The Rubik's Cube was invented in 1974 by Hungarian architect Ernő Rubik.
Hungary's Lake Hévíz is the largest thermal lake in Europe that people can swim in.
Hungarian is closely related to German.
statements.truth: Hungarian is a Uralic language, distantly related to Finnish and Estonian.

statements.text: The Mileștii Mici wine cellars in Moldova hold the largest wine collection in the world, according to Guinness World Records.
Moldova's Orheiul Vechi is a historic site set among limestone cliffs on a tight bend of the Răut River.
Moldova has a long coastline on the Black Sea.
statements.truth: Moldova is landlocked, lying between Romania and Ukraine.

statements.text: Pitch Lake in Trinidad is the largest natural deposit of asphalt in the world.
The steelpan, a drum made from oil barrels, was invented in Trinidad and Tobago.
The limbo dance began in Jamaica.
statements.truth: The limbo dance began on the island of Trinidad.

statements.text: Gabon's Loango National Park is known for 'surfing hippos' that swim in the ocean.
In 2002 Gabon set aside about a tenth of its land as national parks, 13 parks in total.
Gabon was a British colony until 1960.
statements.truth: Gabon was a French colony and became independent from France in 1960.

statements.text: Andorra has two heads of state at once: the Bishop of Urgell in Spain and the President of France.
Catalan is Andorra's only official language.
Andorra la Vella is the lowest capital city in Europe.
statements.truth: At about 1,023 m (3,356 ft), Andorra la Vella is the highest capital city in Europe.

statements.text: Qatar's only land border is with Saudi Arabia.
Khor Al Adaid in Qatar is an 'inland sea' where the Persian Gulf reaches deep into the desert.
Qatar is an island in the Persian Gulf.
statements.truth: Qatar is a peninsula that juts out from the Arabian Peninsula into the Persian Gulf.

statements.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign state in the Americas.
US founding father Alexander Hamilton was born on Nevis.
Saint Kitts' Brimstone Hill Fortress was built by the Spanish.
statements.truth: Brimstone Hill Fortress was designed and built by the British.

statements.text: Brazzaville and Kinshasa, the capitals of two different countries, face each other across the Congo River.
Odzala-Kokoua National Park in the Republic of the Congo is home to many western lowland gorillas.
The Republic of the Congo was once a Belgian colony.
statements.truth: The Republic of the Congo was a French colony, part of French Equatorial Africa. Its neighbour, the DR Congo, was the Belgian colony.

statements.text: The ruins of Spiš Castle form one of the largest castle sites in Slovakia.
Bratislava is the only national capital that borders two other countries: Austria and Hungary.
Slovakia and Czechia split into separate countries in 1968.
statements.truth: Czechoslovakia split peacefully on 1 January 1993, in what became known as the Velvet Divorce.

statements.text: Laos is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia.
Laos's Plain of Jars is scattered with thousands of huge ancient stone jars.
For much of its length, the Mekong forms the border between Laos and Vietnam.
statements.truth: The Mekong forms much of the border between Laos and Thailand, for about 920 km (570 mi).

statements.text: Marie Curie, the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, was born in Warsaw.
Poland's Wieliczka Salt Mine has underground chapels and statues carved by miners out of rock salt.
Poland's Białowieża Forest is home to Europe's last wild tigers.
statements.truth: Białowieża Forest is famous for its European bison, Europe's heaviest land animal.

statements.text: Bulgaria's Rose Valley is famous for producing rose oil for perfumes.
Lactobacillus bulgaricus, a bacterium used to make yogurt, was first identified in 1905 by a Bulgarian doctor.
Bulgarian is written in the Latin alphabet.
statements.truth: Bulgarian is written in Cyrillic, an alphabet that was developed in the First Bulgarian Empire.

statements.text: Romania's Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest is described as the world's heaviest administrative building.
Romanian is a Romance language, descended from Latin.
Most of the Danube Delta lies in Bulgaria.
statements.truth: Most of the Danube Delta lies in Romania, with a small part in Ukraine.

statements.text: Ecuador's name is simply the Spanish word for 'equator'.
Because Earth bulges at the equator, the summit of Ecuador's Chimborazo is the farthest point from Earth's centre.
Panama hats were first made in Panama.
statements.truth: Panama hats come from Ecuador. Many were shipped through Panama on their way to buyers abroad.

statements.text: The dodo, a flightless bird, lived only on Mauritius before it died out in the 1600s.
Mauritius is the only country in Africa where Hinduism is the most practised religion.
Mauritius uses the euro as its currency.
statements.truth: Mauritius uses its own currency, the Mauritian rupee.

statements.text: Singapore is made up of one main island and more than 60 smaller islands and islets.
The name Singapore goes back to a Sanskrit word meaning 'Lion City'.
Singapore lies more than 1,000 km (620 mi) north of the equator.
statements.truth: Singapore is only about 137 km (85 mi) north of the equator.

statements.text: Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell in London's clock tower, not the tower itself.
The London Underground began in 1863 with the world's first underground passenger railway.
Stonehenge was built by the Romans.
statements.truth: Stonehenge was built in prehistoric times, roughly 3000 to 2000 BC, thousands of years before the Romans arrived.

statements.text: Samarkand's Registan square is framed by three grand madrasas.
Itchan Kala, the walled inner town of Khiva in Uzbekistan, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Uzbekistan has a coastline on the Caspian Sea.
statements.truth: Uzbekistan is doubly landlocked: it has no coast, and neither do any of its neighbours.

statements.text: The Great Mosque of Djenné in Mali is the largest mud-brick (adobe) building in the world.
In medieval times, Mali's city of Timbuktu was a renowned centre of learning.
Mali is named after a river that flows through the country.
statements.truth: Mali is named after the Mali Empire, a powerful medieval West African empire.

statements.text: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world by area.
The Pontifical Swiss Guard has protected the popes since 1506.
Vatican City has its own airport.
statements.truth: Vatican City has no airport, though it does have a heliport and a short railway.

statements.text: Bull sharks can swim up rivers into Lake Nicaragua, a freshwater lake.
Ometepe, an island in Lake Nicaragua, is formed by two volcanoes.
Nicaragua is the smallest country in Central America.
statements.truth: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America by area.

statements.text: The Tree of Ténéré in Niger was once called the most isolated tree on Earth, until a truck knocked it down in 1973.
The Ténéré, a vast sandy region of the Sahara in Niger, takes its name from a Tuareg word meaning 'desert'.
Less than a quarter of Niger is covered by the Sahara.
statements.truth: More than 80% of Niger lies in the Sahara Desert.

statements.text: Brunei is split into two separate parts by the Malaysian state of Sarawak.
Kampong Ayer in Brunei's capital is a huge village built on stilts over the water.
Brunei is on the island of Sumatra.
statements.truth: Brunei is on the island of Borneo, which it shares with Malaysia and Indonesia.

statements.text: The word 'robot' comes from R.U.R., a 1920 play by Czech writer Karel Čapek.
Prague's astronomical clock dates back to 1410, and every hour figures of the apostles parade past its windows.
Pilsner beer was first brewed in Germany.
statements.truth: Pilsner was first brewed in 1842 in the Czech city of Plzeň (Pilsen).

statements.text: Tikal in Guatemala was one of the largest cities of the ancient Maya.
Guatemala's currency, the quetzal, is named after its national bird, the resplendent quetzal.
Guatemala's Lake Atitlán was created by a meteorite impact.
statements.truth: Lake Atitlán fills a huge volcanic caldera.

statements.text: Skype was created by a team that included four Estonian developers.
In 2007 Estonia became the first country to allow online voting in a national parliamentary election.
Estonia has fewer than 50 islands.
statements.truth: Estonia has more than 2,000 islands in the Baltic Sea.

statements.text: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.
Algeria's Tassili n'Ajjer plateau holds more than 15,000 prehistoric rock drawings and engravings.
Algeria's capital is Oran.
statements.truth: Algeria's capital and largest city is Algiers. Oran is the country's second-biggest city.

statements.text: K2, the second-highest mountain on Earth, is in the Karakoram range, which runs through northern Pakistan.
Mohenjo-daro, an ancient Indus Valley city in Pakistan, was built around 2500 BC.
Himalayan pink salt is mostly mined in Nepal.
statements.truth: Himalayan salt is mined mainly at the Khewra Salt Mine in Punjab, Pakistan.

statements.text: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world.
The Monaco Grand Prix is raced on the ordinary streets of the city.
Monaco's own citizens are regular players at the Monte Carlo Casino.
statements.truth: Citizens of Monaco are not allowed to gamble in the casino.

statements.text: Costa Rica's 1949 constitution permanently abolished its army.
Costa Rica's Cocos Island, about 550 km (340 mi) offshore, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Costa Rica means 'Rich Forest' in Spanish.
statements.truth: Costa Rica means 'Rich Coast' in Spanish.

statements.text: The Kuwaiti dinar is the highest-valued currency unit in the world.
Kuwait has no permanent rivers or natural lakes.
Kuwait City lies on the coast of the Red Sea.
statements.truth: Kuwait City lies on the Persian Gulf.

statements.text: A green cedar tree sits in the middle of Lebanon's flag.
Byblos in Lebanon is thought to have been continuously inhabited since around 5000 BC.
The Phoenician alphabet, from Lebanon's coast, has no connection to the alphabet used for English.
statements.truth: The Phoenician alphabet is the ancestor of the Greek alphabet, and through it of the Latin alphabet used for English.

statements.text: Suriname is the smallest country in South America.
Suriname is the only independent country outside Europe where Dutch is the main official language.
Most of Suriname is open grassland.
statements.truth: More than 95% of Suriname is covered by rainforest.

statements.text: Belgrade's international airport is named after inventor Nikola Tesla.
Belgrade stands where the Sava River flows into the Danube.
The Iron Gates gorge, on Serbia's border with Romania, was carved by the Rhine.
statements.truth: The Iron Gates gorge was carved by the Danube.

statements.text: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest mountain in Africa.
Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania is rich in fossils and stone tools left by early humans.
Zanzibar, part of Tanzania, became world-famous for growing vanilla.
statements.truth: Zanzibar is famous for its cloves and other spices, which earned it the nickname 'Spice Islands'.

statements.text: Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle.
Lumbini in Nepal is revered as the birthplace of the Buddha.
Mount Everest lies completely inside Nepal.
statements.truth: The summit of Mount Everest sits on the border between Nepal and China.

statements.text: Issyk-Kul, a huge lake high in Kyrgyzstan's mountains, rarely freezes in winter because its water is slightly salty.
The Kyrgyz Epic of Manas is one of the longest epic poems in the world.
Kyrgyzstan's flag shows a blue crescent moon.
statements.truth: Kyrgyzstan's flag is red with a yellow sun, which has 40 rays and the crown of a yurt at its centre.

statements.text: Bahrain is an island country made up of more than 30 islands.
Bahrain's 'Tree of Life' is a mesquite tree, about 400 years old, growing alone in the desert.
Bahrain is linked to Saudi Arabia by a tunnel under the sea.
statements.truth: Bahrain is linked to Saudi Arabia by the King Fahd Causeway, a chain of bridges and embankments about 25 km (16 mi) long.

statements.text: The Richat Structure in Mauritania is a giant set of rings about 40 km (25 mi) wide in the Sahara.
Mauritania's iron ore trains are among the longest and heaviest trains in the world.
Mauritania's capital, Nouakchott, lies in the Sahara far from the sea.
statements.truth: Nouakchott sits on the Atlantic coast.

statements.text: Fiji is made up of more than 300 islands.
Fiji's rugby sevens team won gold at the 2016 Olympics, the country's first Olympic medal.
Fiji's official languages are English and French.
statements.truth: Fiji's official languages are English, Fijian and Hindi.

statements.text: Luxembourg is the world's only remaining grand duchy.
In 2020 Luxembourg became the first country to make public transport free nationwide.
French is Luxembourg's only official language.
statements.truth: Luxembourg uses three languages officially: Luxembourgish, French and German.

statements.text: In 2011 Samoa moved to the other side of the International Date Line, skipping 30 December entirely.
The English word 'tattoo' comes from the Samoan word 'tatau', meaning 'to strike'.
Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island, is buried in Scotland.
statements.truth: Stevenson died in Samoa in 1894 and is buried on Mount Vaea, on the island of Upolu.

statements.text: The remains of more than 2,000 ancient temples and pagodas survive at Bagan in Myanmar.
The name of Yangon's Shwedagon Pagoda means 'Golden Dagon Pagoda'.
The fishermen of Myanmar's Inle Lake are famous for rowing with their arms only.
statements.truth: Inle Lake's fishermen are known for rowing with one leg wrapped around the oar.

statements.text: The welwitschia, a desert plant found in Namibia and Angola, can live for more than 1,000 years.
The Hoba meteorite in Namibia is the largest known meteorite still in one piece.
The Namib Desert is one of the youngest deserts in the world.
statements.truth: The Namib may be the oldest desert in the world, having been dry or nearly dry for around 55 to 80 million years.

statements.text: Lithuanian is considered one of the most archaic living Indo-European languages.
By 2006, Lithuania's Hill of Crosses was estimated to hold about 100,000 crosses.
Ice hockey is considered Lithuania's national sport.
statements.truth: Basketball is by far the most popular sport in Lithuania.

statements.text: On a beach in the Exuma islands of the Bahamas, wild pigs swim out to meet visiting boats.
Dean's Blue Hole in the Bahamas is one of the deepest blue holes in the world, about 202 m (663 ft) deep.
The Bahamas is made up of fewer than 50 islands.
statements.truth: The Bahamas has about 700 islands and more than 2,500 cays.

statements.text: LEGO comes from Denmark, and its name comes from the Danish 'leg godt', meaning 'play well'.
Denmark's flag, the Dannebrog, is thought to be the oldest national flag still in use.
Copenhagen's Little Mermaid statue is based on a Viking legend.
statements.truth: The statue is based on a fairy tale by Danish author Hans Christian Andersen.

statements.text: More than 90% of Tajikistan is covered by mountains.
Tajikistan's Fedchenko Glacier is the longest glacier in the world outside the polar regions.
Tajik is a Turkic language, like Uzbek and Kazakh.
statements.truth: Tajik is a form of Persian.

statements.text: Cameroon is often called 'Africa in miniature' because of its varied landscapes and cultures.
Mount Cameroon, an active volcano, is the highest point in sub-Saharan western and central Africa.
French is Cameroon's only official language.
statements.truth: Cameroon has two official languages, French and English.

statements.text: Millions of golden jellyfish migrate across Palau's Jellyfish Lake every day.
In 2009 Palau created the world's first shark sanctuary.
Palau uses the Japanese yen as its currency.
statements.truth: Palau uses the US dollar.

statements.text: Dominica's Boiling Lake is the second-largest hot lake in the world.
Dominica's flag features a sisserou parrot, the national bird.
Dominica was named after a French saint called Dominic.
statements.truth: Christopher Columbus named it Dominica, from the Latin for 'Sunday', because he first saw it on a Sunday in November 1493.

statements.text: Dubai's Burj Khalifa skyscraper is about 830 m (2,722 ft) tall.
The United Arab Emirates is a federation of seven emirates.
Dubai's palm-shaped Palm Jumeirah is a natural island.
statements.truth: Palm Jumeirah is an artificial archipelago, built by reclaiming land from the sea.

statements.text: Ships crossing the Panama Canal are lifted by locks to Gatun Lake, 26 m (85 ft) above sea level.
Panama uses the US dollar alongside its own currency, the balboa.
The Panama Canal opened in 1950.
statements.truth: The Panama Canal opened in 1914.

statements.text: Johannes Gutenberg developed the movable-type printing press in Mainz around 1440.
Much of Germany's autobahn network has no fixed speed limit, only an advisory one.
Neuschwanstein Castle was built in the Middle Ages.
statements.truth: Neuschwanstein was built in the 19th century for King Ludwig II of Bavaria, starting in 1869.

statements.text: Tonga never gave up its sovereignty to any foreign power.
Tonga is made up of 171 islands, of which 45 are inhabited.
Tonga is a republic led by an elected president.
statements.truth: Tonga is a kingdom, a semi-constitutional monarchy with a king as head of state.

statements.text: The Niger, Gambia and Senegal rivers all begin in Guinea's highlands.
Guinea is roughly the same size as the United Kingdom.
Guinea's capital is Bamako.
statements.truth: Guinea's capital is Conakry, on the Atlantic coast. Bamako is the capital of neighbouring Mali.

statements.text: Thanks to its overseas territories, France uses 12 time zones, more than any other country.
The cave paintings at Lascaux in France are thought to be around 17,000 to 22,000 years old.
The Eiffel Tower was always meant to be a permanent monument.
statements.truth: It was built as a temporary structure for the 1889 World's Fair and was due to be taken down in 1909. It was saved because it proved useful for radio.

statements.text: The world's first underwater sculpture park opened off Grenada in 2006.
Grenada is nicknamed the 'Island of Spice' for its nutmeg and other spices.
Grenada's capital is Castries.
statements.truth: Grenada's capital is St. George's. Castries is the capital of Saint Lucia.

statements.text: The coelacanth, a fish once thought extinct for millions of years, lives in the waters around the Comoros.
Mount Karthala, on Grande Comore, is a very active volcano that has erupted more than 20 times since the 1800s.
The Comoros lies in the Atlantic Ocean, off West Africa.
statements.truth: The Comoros lies in the Indian Ocean, in the Mozambique Channel between Mozambique and Madagascar.

statements.text: Kuala Lumpur's Petronas Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.
Sarawak Chamber, in a Malaysian cave, is the largest known cave chamber in the world by area.
Malaysia's capital, Kuala Lumpur, is on the island of Borneo.
statements.truth: Kuala Lumpur is on the Malay Peninsula. Malaysia's states on Borneo are a separate part of the country.

statements.text: About 840 living languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea, the most linguistically diverse country in the world.
The hooded pitohui of Papua New Guinea is one of the few known poisonous birds.
Papua New Guinea shares its main island with Australia.
statements.truth: Papua New Guinea shares the island of New Guinea with Indonesia.

statements.text: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world.
Bolivia has two capitals: Sucre is the constitutional capital and La Paz is the seat of government.
Spanish is Bolivia's only official language.
statements.truth: Spanish is the main official language, but 36 Indigenous languages also have official status.

statements.text: The Darvaza gas crater in Turkmenistan, nicknamed the 'Door to Hell', has been burning since around 1971.
Turkmenistan's Akhal-Teke horses are famous for the metallic shine of their coats.
Most of Turkmenistan is covered by grassland.
statements.truth: About 70% of Turkmenistan is covered by the Karakum Desert.

statements.text: Côte d'Ivoire, meaning 'Ivory Coast', was named by European traders in the 1400s and 1500s after the ivory trade along its shore.
The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace in Yamoussoukro is one of the largest churches in the world.
Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire's largest city, is also its official capital.
statements.truth: Yamoussoukro is the official capital. Abidjan is the largest city and the main economic hub.

statements.text: Montenegro uses the euro, even though it is not part of the eurozone.
Montenegro's winding Bay of Kotor is the drowned valley of a river that has since vanished.
The name Montenegro means 'Green Mountain'.
statements.truth: Montenegro means 'Black Mountain'.

statements.text: At about 21 km² (8 sq mi), Nauru is the third-smallest country in the world.
Nauru has no official capital, though its parliament sits in Yaren.
Nauru's interior is untouched rainforest.
statements.truth: Nauru is a phosphate-rock island, and most of its interior was strip-mined for phosphate for about a century from 1900.

statements.text: Saudi Arabia has no rivers that flow all year round.
The Rub' al Khali, or Empty Quarter, is the largest continuous sand desert in the world.
Saudi Arabia's ancient tombs at Hegra were carved by the Romans.
statements.truth: Hegra was built by the Nabataeans, and most of its remains date from their kingdom.

statements.text: In land diving, a ritual on Vanuatu's Pentecost Island, men leap from tall wooden towers with only vines tied to their ankles.
Hideaway Island in Vanuatu has one of the world's few underwater post offices.
Vanuatu's official languages are English and Spanish.
statements.truth: Vanuatu's official languages are Bislama, English and French.

statements.text: Burundi lies on the shore of Lake Tanganyika, one of the deepest lakes in the world.
In 2019 Burundi made Gitega its political capital, in place of Bujumbura.
Burundi's flag shows a large black eagle.
statements.truth: Burundi's flag has a white diagonal cross with three red stars in a white circle in the middle.

statements.text: Kaieteur Falls in Guyana has a single drop of about 226 m (741 ft).
Guyana was the British colony of British Guiana until it became independent in 1966.
Guyana's name comes from a Spanish word meaning 'gold'.
statements.truth: The name Guyana is thought to come from an Indigenous word meaning 'land of many waters'.

statements.text: Every summer, Mostar holds a traditional diving competition from its Stari Most bridge.
Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics.
Bosnia and Herzegovina is landlocked.
statements.truth: Bosnia and Herzegovina has a short stretch of Adriatic coast around the town of Neum, its only access to the sea.

statements.text: Kiribati's islands stretch into all four hemispheres: north, south, east and west.
Kiribati's Kiritimati, or Christmas Island, is one of the world's largest atolls by land area.
Kiribati's capital is a single large island.
statements.truth: Kiribati's capital, Tarawa, is made up of a string of islets linked by causeways.

statements.text: The grapefruit is believed to have first appeared in Barbados.
Mount Gay in Barbados, dating from 1703, is one of the oldest rum makers in the world.
Barbados is a volcanic island.
statements.truth: Barbados is made mostly of coral limestone, unlike its volcanic neighbours.

statements.text: Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the largest religious complex in the world.
Cambodia's flag shows a picture of Angkor Wat.
Cambodia's Tonlé Sap lake stays the same size all year round.
statements.truth: In the rainy season the Tonlé Sap river reverses its flow, and the lake swells to several times its dry-season size.

statements.text: Slovenia's Postojna Cave is home to the olm, a blind salamander that lives in underground waters.
About 60% of Slovenia is covered by forest.
Slovenia has no coastline.
statements.truth: Slovenia has a short coastline, about 47 km (29 mi) long, on the Adriatic Sea.

statements.text: Chad is named after Lake Chad.
Emi Koussi, in Chad's Tibesti Mountains, is the highest point in the Sahara.
Lake Chad grew much larger between 1960 and 1980.
statements.truth: Lake Chad shrank dramatically: its open water fell from about 25,000 km² in 1960 to about 2,000 km² in 1980.

statements.text: Yanar Dag, near Baku, is a hillside where a natural gas fire burns nonstop.
Gobustan National Park in Azerbaijan holds thousands of ancient rock carvings.
Azerbaijan's capital, Baku, lies on the shore of the Black Sea.
statements.truth: Baku lies on the Caspian Sea.

statements.text: By 2019, about 8% of Tuvalu's government revenue came from royalties on its internet domain, .tv.
Tuvalu covers only about 26 km² (10 sq mi) of land.
The name Tuvalu means 'one island'.
statements.truth: Tuvalu means 'eight standing together', because eight of its nine islands were inhabited.

statements.text: More than 170,000 concrete bunkers were built across Albania between the 1960s and the 1980s.
In Albanian, the country is called Shqipëria.
Albania's flag shows a white dove on a blue background.
statements.truth: Albania's flag shows a black double-headed eagle on a red background.

statements.text: Cuba's bee hummingbird is the smallest bird in the world.
Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.
Havana lies on Cuba's south coast, facing the Caribbean Sea.
statements.truth: Havana is on Cuba's northern side, rising from the Straits of Florida.

statements.text: Senegal's Lake Retba, or Lac Rose, is famous for its pink water, caused by algae.
The African Renaissance Monument in Dakar is the tallest statue in Africa.
Senegal's capital, Dakar, sits near the easternmost point of Africa.
statements.truth: Dakar is on the Cap-Vert peninsula, the westernmost point of mainland Africa.

statements.text: Equatorial Guinea is the only country in sub-Saharan Africa where Spanish is an official language.
Equatorial Guinea's Bioko Island used to be called Fernando Po.
The equator runs right through Equatorial Guinea's mainland.
statements.truth: The equator does not cross its land. It passes through the country's waters, about 1.4° north of the island of Annobón.

statements.text: Livraria Bertrand in Lisbon, founded in 1732, is the oldest bookshop in the world still operating, according to Guinness World Records.
Portugal produces about half of the world's cork.
Pastel de nata custard tarts were invented by bakers in Brazil.
statements.truth: Pastéis de nata were created by monks at the Jerónimos Monastery in Belém, Lisbon.

statements.text: The Maldives is the lowest country in the world, with an average height of just 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in) above sea level.
The Maldives is made up of about 1,200 coral islands grouped into 26 atolls.
The Maldives lies in the Pacific Ocean.
statements.truth: The Maldives lies in the Indian Ocean, south-west of Sri Lanka and India.

statements.text: The bikini swimsuit is named after Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands.
Marshallese navigators used stick charts to map ocean swells.
The Marshall Islands are named after a Marshallese chief.
statements.truth: The islands are named after British captain John Marshall, who explored the region in 1788.

statements.text: Uruguay hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup, in 1930.
The 'Sun of May' on Uruguay's flag has 16 rays.
Uruguay's capital, Montevideo, lies on the Pacific coast.
statements.truth: Montevideo lies on the Río de la Plata, which opens into the Atlantic Ocean.

statements.text: In Greek mythology, the goddess Aphrodite was born from the sea off the coast of Cyprus.
The flag of Cyprus shows a map of the island.
Halloumi cheese originally comes from Italy.
statements.truth: Halloumi comes from Cyprus, where it has been made for centuries.

statements.text: East Rennell in the Solomon Islands is the largest raised coral atoll in the world.
More than 70 languages are spoken across the Solomon Islands archipelago.
The Solomon Islands got their name from British sailors in the 1800s.
statements.truth: The name goes back to the 1500s: after Spanish navigator Álvaro de Mendaña visited in 1568, people who heard of his voyage began calling the islands 'the Solomons'.

statements.text: Reggae music developed in Jamaica in the late 1960s.
Ackee and saltfish is Jamaica's national dish.
Jamaica's flag has red, white and blue stripes.
statements.truth: Jamaica's flag has a gold diagonal cross, with green triangles at the top and bottom and black ones at the sides.

statements.text: Cape Verde's islands were uninhabited when Portuguese sailors arrived in the 15th century.
Pico do Fogo, the volcano on Cape Verde's island of Fogo, erupted as recently as 2014.
Cape Verde's most famous singer, Cesária Évora, was known as the 'Queen of Fado'.
statements.truth: Cesária Évora sang morna, Cape Verde's own soulful music, and was nicknamed the 'Barefoot Diva'.

statements.text: About a third of the plants on Yemen's Socotra island are found nowhere else on Earth.
Shibam in Yemen is famous for its mud-brick tower houses and is nicknamed the 'Manhattan of the desert'.
Mocha coffee takes its name from a city in Brazil.
statements.truth: Mocha is named after the port city of Mocha in Yemen, long known for its coffee trade.

statements.text: Riga's Central Market is housed in old German Zeppelin hangars.
Latvia's carmine red and white flag is one of the oldest flags in the world.
Latvian is a Slavic language closely related to Russian.
statements.truth: Latvian is a Baltic language, most closely related to Lithuanian.

statements.text: Nan Madol, an ancient ruined city off Pohnpei in Micronesia, was built on 92 artificial islets.
On Yap, in Micronesia, giant stone discs called rai have long been used as money.
The Federated States of Micronesia is a single large island.
statements.truth: Micronesia is spread over 607 islands, grouped into four states.

statements.text: Sierra Leone's capital, Freetown, was founded as a home for formerly enslaved Africans.
Fourah Bay College in Freetown, founded in 1827, was the first Western-style university in sub-Saharan Africa.
Sierra Leone's name comes from French words meaning 'silver coast'.
statements.truth: The name comes from 'Serra Leoa', Portuguese for 'Lioness Mountains', given by an explorer in 1462.

statements.text: El Salvador is the smallest country on the American mainland.
Joya de Cerén, a Maya farming village buried by a volcanic eruption, is called the 'Pompeii of the Americas'.
El Salvador has coastlines on both the Pacific and the Caribbean.
statements.truth: El Salvador is the only Central American country with no Caribbean coastline. Its coast is on the Pacific.

statements.text: Hangul, the Korean alphabet, was created in the 15th century under King Sejong the Great.
The haenyeo of South Korea's Jeju Island are women divers who dive up to 20 m (66 ft) for seafood while holding their breath.
Kimchi is traditionally made mostly from fermented carrots.
statements.truth: Kimchi is usually made from salted and fermented napa cabbage and Korean radish.
